body.x: Awesomenics Inc. (CEO JEONG WOO YOEL) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Awesomenics is a business that designs and manufactures heat-releasing test pins for consumable components to determine whether system semiconductors are defective. As global semiconductor technology evolves and various development and manufacturing businesses compete in high integration, there is an emerging technical need to effectively release heat from semiconductors. That is why Awesomenics is gaining attention from the industry as a provider of pins that can reduce testing costs for manufacturing.

While existing pins were manufactured by combining four components to assemble a single test pin, Awesomenics' pins can be made with three instead. Thanks to its component simplification, their pins cut down the cost of components, as well as reduce lead time.

In addition, their test pins enhance the electrical properties with an electrical flow that has gone through three steps, as well as consequently increase the quality of the system semiconductors. It emits heat through variable slits placed in the exterior and the space of the spring, ensuring excellent heat dissipation.

“We hope to meet global semiconductor manufacturers, design corporations, and testing houses, such as Qualcomm, Intel, and NVIDIA, for tech meetings,” stated an Awesomenics representative. They added, “We also are looking for investors who can propose a $1-$2.8 million investment.”

“Our plan does not stop at the current test pin but extends to developing heat releasing test sockets and presenting them to the market in the future,” explained the representative. “We want to contribute to the growth of global semiconductor technology with our solution to save costs in the system semiconductor manufacturing process.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
